briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF M-015
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- water tower top: (62, 67), roof
- north roof: (-36, 77), roof
- control room: (102, -149), indoor
- workshop: (-129, -140), indoor
- east fence: (-18, -133), outdoor
- site B: (46, 33), outdoor
- parking lot: (-143, 76), outdoor

Robots:
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1380 s, including the return to its start.
- D2 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 9.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1260 s, including the return to its start.
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 9 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3000 s, including the return to its start.
- D3 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 7.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1380 s, including the return to its start.
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 3 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 16 kg), camera, thermal camera. Endurance: 3660 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Replace the filter cartridge at control room. Location: control room. Duration: 150 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T2: Inspect north roof with a camera. Location: north roof. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 240 s.
- T3: Run a thermal scan of water tower top. Location: water tower top. Duration: 180 s. Needs: thermal camera.
- T4: Deliver the toolkit (12 kg) to parking lot. Location: parking lot. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 12 kg).
- T5: Run a thermal scan of parking lot. Location: parking lot. Duration: 180 s. Needs: thermal camera.
- T6: Replace the filter cartridge at control room. Location: control room. Duration: 300 s. Needs: robotic arm. Deadline: finished by t = 1380 s.
- T7: Replace the filter cartridge at workshop. Location: workshop. Duration: 240 s. Needs: robotic arm. Deadline: finished by t = 900 s. Can start only after T10 is finished.
- T8: Collect a soil sample (1 kg) at parking lot and keep it on board. Location: parking lot. Duration: 90 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 1 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 480 s.
- T9: Deliver the first-aid kit (7 kg) to parking lot. Location: parking lot. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 7 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 180 s.
- T10: Deliver the toolkit (13 kg) to workshop. Location: workshop. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 13 kg).

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 1800 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Hi team, here is today's job at the site.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: water tower top (62, 67, a rooftop); north roof (-36, 77, a rooftop); control room (102, -149, indoors); workshop (-129, -140, indoors); east fence (-18, -133, outside); site B (46, 33, outside); parking lot (-143, 76, outside).

The fleet: D1, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera, cruises at 8.5 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 23 minutes of flight time, return trip included. D2 is a quadcopter at base with a camera and a thermal camera; it flies at 9.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 21 minutes including the flight home. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 9 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 50 minutes including getting back. D3 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 7.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 23 minutes including the flight home. G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 16 kg at 3 m/s and runs for 61 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera and a thermal camera.

Jobs:
(T1) Change the filter at control room - that takes 2.5 minutes on site.
(T2) Do a visual check of north roof - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 4 minutes.
(T3) Do a heat check over water tower top - that takes 3 minutes on site.
(T4) Drop the toolkit off at parking lot; it weighs 12 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T5) Look for overheating equipment around parking lot - that takes 3 minutes on site.
(T6) Swap the filter cartridge at control room - that takes 5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 23 minutes.
(T7) Swap the filter cartridge at workshop - that takes 4 minutes on site but only once the toolkit (T10) has arrived and it has to be finished within the first 15 minutes.
(T8) Pick up a soil sample at parking lot and keep it on board; it weighs 1 kg - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 8 minutes.
(T9) Get the first-aid kit (7 kg) over to parking lot - that takes 0.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 3 minutes.
(T10) Drop the toolkit off at workshop; it weighs 13 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 30 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
